Infection was associated with increased expression of genes involved in bacterial attachment and adaptation, together with reduced activity of genes linked to metabolism. These findings provide direct evidence that S. epidermidis adapts its behavior to the host environment during infection and identify bacterial processes that may contribute to the transition from commensalism to pathogenicity.

Microbiology Spectrum.title: An engineered Zika virus recombinant adenovirus vaccine induces protective immune response in mice.
Microbiology Spectrum.abstract: [UNLABELLED] Zika virus (ZIKV), Japanese encephalitis virus (JEV), and dengue virus (DENV) co-circulate in many countries/territories. Our previous publication reported that the antibodies (Abs) induced by ZIKV infection could exacerbate the mortality of JEV-infected mice, bringing challenges to the development of traditional Zika vaccines. Here, we developed two recombinant adenoviruses (Ad5-ZIKV-EWT and Ad5-ZIKV-Emut) encoding the ZIKV wild-type E protein and an E protein mutant carrying five amino acid substitutions (replaced by alanine) in the bc loop and fusion loop regions of the E protein, respectively. The levels of JEV-cross-reactive or DENV-cross-reactive Ab responses induced by Ad5-ZIKV-Emut immunization in mice are lower than those induced by Ad5-ZIKV-EWT. The level of ZIKV-neutralizing Abs induced by Ad5-ZIKV-Emut is comparable to that elicited by Ad5-ZIKV-EWT. The ability of Abs induced by Ad5-ZIKV-Emut to enhance JEV or DENV infections in vitro is attenuated as compared with that induced by Ad5-ZIKV-EWT. The in vivo protective role of Abs induced by Ad5-ZIKV-Emut is similar to that induced by Ad5-ZIKV-EWT. Mice receiving Ad5-ZIKV-EWT-immune mouse sera exhibited antibody-dependent enhancement (ADE) post-DENV challenge, whereas passively transferred Ad5-ZIKV-Emut-immune mouse sera did not lead to obvious ADE of DENV infection in recipient mice. Notably, maternally acquired Abs did not enhance the mortality of 2-day-old neonates born to Ad5-ZIKV-Emut-immunized mice post-JEV challenge. These results suggest that optimizing the E protein amino acid sequence of ZIKV could significantly reduce the level of cross-reactive Abs to JEV and DENV, and abrogate the ADE of JEV and DENV infections, providing a promising strategy to develop an effective and safe ZIKV vaccine. [IMPORTANCE] Zika virus (ZIKV), Japanese encephalitis virus (JEV), and dengue virus (DENV) co-circulate in some countries or territories. The results of preliminary animal experiments and clinical cohort studies support that antibodies induced by ZIKV infection can enhance JEV or DENV infection in vitro and in vivo. Therefore, the ZIKV vaccine encoding the wild-type E protein constructed by conventional methods has the antibody-dependent enhancement risk against JEV and DENV infections. In this study, we obtained an E protein mutant by mutating key amino acids in the bc loop and FL sequences of the ZIKV wild-type E protein to alanine. The recombinant adenovirus vaccine based on this E protein mutant is not only effective but also safer in preventing ZIKV infection in the future.

Microbiology Spectrum.title: Comparative symptomatology and aggressiveness of bacterial mycopathogens on button mushroom.
Microbiology Spectrum.abstract: [UNLABELLED] Bacterial diseases have fundamental effects on the productivity of the edible mushroom industry. A group of diverse bacterial agents, including both gram-negative and gram-positive species, induce diseases on mushroom caps. In this study, we investigated the symptomatology, aggressiveness, and competitiveness of a comprehensive range of bacterial mycopathogens isolated from button mushroom (Agaricus bisporus) on mushroom caps. The bacterial agents used in our assays involved five Pseudomonas species, the corynebacterial species Mycetocola saprophilus, as well as the multifaceted species Burkholderia gladioli, Ewingella americana, and Cedecea neteri. Comparative symptomatology of all bacterial species on mushroom caps showed that Pseudomonas tolaasii, Burkholderia gladioli, Mycetocola saprophilus, and Ewingella americana induced the most severe symptoms. Two-by-two co-inoculation of the latter species onto mushroom caps showed that B. gladioli had dominance on the caps, outcompeting the other three species. Plate-based antibiosis assays also showed remarkable antagonistic activity between different mycopathogenic bacteria, attesting to their competitive behavior on mushroom caps. Electron microscopy of the infected cap tissues revealed substantial morphological differences between the hyphal mass colonized by each bacterial pathogen, where B. gladioli-induced dehydration and blistering on hyphal surfaces, while P. tolaasii induced breakdown of the intercellular matrix and separation of the hyphae in the proximity of the invading bacteria. Our data provide novel insight into the comparative symptomatology and aggressiveness of bacterial mycopathogens on button mushrooms under experimental conditions. [IMPORTANCE] Commercial production of edible mushrooms faces various biotic constraints, including bacterial, fungal, and viral pathogens, which collectively reduce quality, shelf life, and marketability of the product. While fungal pathogens might have more destructive effects on mushroom caps, bacterial agents possess higher biological and taxonomic diversity in production facilities, extending their negative effect from mushroom farm to post-harvest processing stage and marketplaces. Bacterial blotch or brown blotch is a generic name assigned to a set of bacterial diseases characterized by cap discoloration, sunken tissues, or brown spots. This study highlights the biological importance of co-occurrence of different mycopathogenic bacteria on mushroom caps, investigating their potential competition and antibiosis in a controlled experimental condition. Results obtained in this study would shed light on the biological complexity of bacterial communities associated with mushroom caps, paving the way for sustainable management of blotch disease.

Environmental Science & Technology.title: Correction to "Application of the Biological Toxicity Effect Ratio (BER) Method for Advancing Water Quality Criteria Derivation".
60 Years of ES&T in Pursuit of Sustainable Systems.
Energy Supply and Demand Coordination Can Advance Both Climate Goals and Sustainable Development in the Global South.
Environmental Science & Technology.abstract: Reconciling climate mitigation with sustainable development is a critical imperative in the Global South, where rising emissions coincide with persistent development deficits. Here, we develop an integrated assessment framework linking nationally determined contribution (NDC)-aligned supply-side, demand-side, and coordinated supply-demand policy packages to greenhouse-gas trajectories and a six-goal Sustainable Development Goal (SDG) scorecard. We show that supply-focused renewable expansion or demand-focused efficiency improves selected SDG-related dimensions but creates trade-offs involving energy-cost pressure, water use, and ecosystem protection. By comparison, an integrated supply-demand strategy maximizes the SDG score (69 versus 65 under REF in 2050), enhances clean-energy penetration and efficiency, and averts approximately 485,000 annual premature deaths in 2050 relative to REF. These findings highlight the potential of coordinated supply-demand strategies to reduce climate-SDG trade-offs across the Global South.

Environmental Science & Technology.title: Divalent Cations and Chlorine Synergistically Reshape T6SS-Mediated Microbial Competition in Water Distribution System Biofilms.
Environmental Science & Technology.abstract: Microbial interactions shape the community structure and function in drinking water distribution system (DWDS) biofilms, yet how the dynamic competition is regulated in biofilms remains poorly understood. Here, we show that divalent cations (Ca2+, Mg2+) and chlorine in drinking water synergistically activate the type VI secretion system (T6SS) in opportunistic pathogens within biofilms. Field-collected biofilms serve as ecological hotspots that selectively enrich specific T6SS-harboring pathogens. Using simulated pipe systems and mutant validation, we further establish that divalent cations and chlorine enhance c-di-GMP signaling to promote T6SS-mediated colonization. This activation stimulates EPS production, whose polysaccharides mitigate T6SS attack, dampening the competitive advantage during mid-stage maturation but allowing gradual resurgence over extended succession. This divalent cation-chlorine-driven interplay shapes ecological succession, selectively retaining T6SS-proficient cells and establishing a "biofilm reservoir effect." Under chlorine decay, T6SS-active pathogens can be released into bulk water, elevating exposure risks. Conversely, reducing divalent cations via nanofiltration suppresses T6SS across multiple pathogens, limiting reservoir accumulation and release. Our findings identify divalent cation availability as a key environmental signal associated with T6SS-mediated competition, linking water chemistry to pathogen persistence. This work suggests integrating membrane-based divalent cation removal with chlorine management as a chemistry-based strategy to mitigate microbial risks, advancing an integrated water quality paradigm for drinking water safety.

Environmental Science & Technology.title: Structure-Dependent Maternal-Fetal Transfer and Fetal Hepatic Accumulation of PFOA and Hexafluoropropylene Oxide (HFPO)-Based Alternatives: Implications for Fetal Liver Metabolic Disruption.
Environmental Science & Technology.abstract: Hexafluoropropylene oxide (HFPO)-based compounds have been increasingly adopted as replacements for legacy per- and polyfluoroalkyl substances (PFAS) such as perfluorooctanoic acid (PFOA), yet evidence on developmental toxicity remains limited. This study investigated structure-dependent maternal-fetal transfer, fetal tissue distribution, and hepatic effects of PFOA and four HFPO-based alternatives, including hexafluoropropylene oxide dimer acid (HFPO-DA) and hexafluoropropylene oxide trimer acid (HFPO-TA) homologues, in gestational mice. All compounds were detected in maternal serum, fetal tissues, and amniotic fluid in a dose-dependent manner, but transplacental transfer efficiencies varied markedly. C9 HFPO-TA showed the greatest fetal accumulation, indicating enhanced fetal retention. Desorption electrospray ionization mass spectrometry imaging revealed preferential hepatic localization of PFOA and HFPO trimers, with fetal hepatic burden increasing with van der Waals volume, suggesting structure-dependent enrichment. Metabolomics showed broad alterations of fetal hepatic metabolism, dominated by altered lipids and lipid-like molecules. 5-Aminolevulinic acid, a key heme precursor, was consistently reduced, whereas ALAS1 and ALAD protein levels increased, indicating perturbation of heme biosynthesis. The provisional, study-specific developmental reference doses derived from fetal or placental endpoints were comparable to or lower than those based on maternal hepatomegaly, suggesting greater developmental sensitivity. These findings reveal structure-dependent fetal liver accumulation and support incorporating fetal-specific endpoints into PFAS risk assessment.

Environmental Science & Technology.title: Can the Spatial Planning of Livestock Production Tackle Future Nitrogen Pollution in China?
Environmental Science & Technology.abstract: Nitrogen (N) pollution from livestock production significantly threatens China's air and water quality, necessitating innovative solutions to balance food security and environmental sustainability. Studies have mostly overlooked the spatial heterogeneity of N-related environmental impacts and the trade-offs between reducing ammonia (NH3) emissions and N concentrations in water. This study develops a spatially explicit multiscale model system encompassing 13,000 polygons across China to assess soil N balance, NH3 emission intensity, and N concentrations in surface water, aiming to explore integrated spatial-planning (SP) strategies that maximize synergy and minimize trade-offs. Our findings reveal that single-purpose SP scenarios (e.g., reducing NH3 emissions or instream N concentrations) can effectively address one N-related issue but produce substantial trade-offs, leaving >50% of China's population exposed to at least another N-related problem. However, an integrated SP approach could reduce harmful N exposures for 90% of China's population while ensuring food security. This approach involves reallocating 14% of livestock production, reducing livestock numbers by one-third relative to the 2050 baseline, and implementing advanced technologies to mitigate N pollution hotspots. Thus, our findings emphasize the importance of spatially explicit N boundaries and multicriteria planning to tackle N pollution in air and water simultaneously, supporting cross-media N management policy-making and region-specific strategies.

Environmental Science & Technology.title: Genetic Background and Metabolic Influence on Long-Term Lithium Bioaccumulation in Mytilus Mussels and Their Hybrids.
Environmental Science & Technology.abstract: Marine mussels are widely used as sentinel organisms in coastal biomonitoring, yet the biological mechanisms controlling the bioaccumulation of emerging metals remain poorly constrained. Climate change and anthropogenic disturbances are reshaping species distributions and contact zones, promoting mussel hybridization that may alter physiological traits and contaminant-handling capacities. Lithium (Li) remains largely overlooked despite its potential toxicity and rapidly increasing global demand. Here, we investigate the influence of critical factors on Li bioaccumulation by mussels combining genetic background and isotopic approaches. Progenies of two Mytilus species and their hybrids were transplanted to the same Atlantic coastal site for 12 months. Over this in situ exposure period, Li concentrations show comparable temporal trends across all progeny groups, with an initial uptake-dominated phase followed by biodilution. Lithium isotope ratios (δ7Li) display a coherent temporal trend across all groups (decrease at early exposure, increase during later growth), and the magnitude of the shift differs slightly among genetic backgrounds. Across samples, δ7Li is coupled to growth-related metrics (dry weight) and inversely related to Li concentrations, indicating a metabolic control on Li isotope compositions of these organisms. Li concentrations are also positively correlated with lithogenic-associated elements (e.g., aluminum), consistent with the influence of particle associated Li. A simplified biodynamic modeling including Li isotopes data further indicates a more efficient Li depuration after 5 months, combined with a relatively stronger contribution from dissolved Li. Overall, growth-related factors emerged as the primary biological drivers of Li concentration and isotope variability, with the relative contributions of dissolved and particulate exposure pathways varying in association with physiological growth. Hybridization may modulate Li bioaccumulation and δ7Li values, but its influence appears secondary and does not compromise the use of Mytilus mussels as bioindicators in established frameworks such as "Mussel Watch".

Environmental Science & Technology.title: Building-Stock Turnover Reshapes Mitigation Priorities in China's Building Sector.
Environmental Science & Technology.abstract: China's building sector is pivotal to the 2060 carbon-neutrality ambition, yet prospective assessments often insufficiently capture regional heterogeneity and life-cycle emission dynamics. Here, we develop a provincial-level dynamic framework integrating material flow analysis, life-cycle assessment, and machine-learning-informed parameter trajectories to project emissions through 2060. Under a business-as-usual (BAU) scenario, China's building life-cycle emissions are projected to peak in 2031-2033, while carbon neutrality remains challenged by persistent pressures from both material use and building operations. These pressures arise from the existing stock, whose continued use sustains energy demand while increasing building retirements shift construction from stock growth to the replacement of retired buildings. Implementing a high-efficiency scenario with regionally differentiated deployment of material- and energy-efficiency strategies could reduce China's building-sector life-cycle emissions by 90% in 2060 relative to the BAU scenario. Provincial analysis further reveals that similar overall mitigation potential masks substantial differences in the composition of effective mitigation portfolios, reflecting local building-stock and energy-use characteristics. To close the remaining gap, deeper operational decarbonization should be coupled with stock-management strategies that extend building lifetimes, avoid premature demolition, and prioritize renovation and reuse.

Environmental Science & Technology.title: Slippery Amphiphilic Antifouling Loose Nanofiltration Membrane with "Double-Defense" Functionalities for High-Salinity Organic Wastewater Sustainable Management.
Environmental Science & Technology.abstract: Loose nanofiltration (LNF) holds potential for sustainable management of high-salinity organic wastewater through precise organics/salts fractionation, but practical application is constrained by severe organic-inorganic combined fouling. Herein, we propose a "double-defense" antifouling strategy and develop a slippery amphiphilic LNF membrane via facile stepwise surface modification. A hydrophilic branched polyethylenimine (PEI) network was first cross-linked onto a polyamide (PA) substrate to form a fouling-resistant protection layer, followed by covalent grafting of liquid-like polydimethylsiloxane (PDMS) brushes to confer a slippery, fouling-release surface. The PEI layer acts as a hydration and electrostatic barrier to repel organic-cation complexes and scale precursors, while the slippery PDMS layer with high mobility and low surface energy minimizes interfacial interactions and strengthens hydraulic shear responsiveness. During the concentration of authentic leachate membrane bioreactor (MBR) effluent, the optimized membrane showed superior antifouling performance: low flux decline ratio (FDR) of 41.6% and high flux recovery ratio (FRR) of 98.1%, outperforming a commercial PA membrane (FDR 91.2%, FRR 78.4%). It also delivered an organics/salts fractionation selectivity 7.8 times that of the commercial membrane, demonstrating multiple cycles stability. This rationally designed architecture offers a practical solution for challenging wastewater and is extensible to other PA-based membrane systems in environmental applications.

Environmental Science & Technology.title: From Nontargeted Analysis to Toxicity: Revealing the Disinfection Byproduct Exposome.
Environmental Science & Technology.abstract: Chemical disinfection is essential for ensuring the microbiological safety of drinking water, but it inevitably generates disinfection byproducts (DBPs), introducing a complex and largely unresolved chemical burden. Trihalomethanes (THMs) and haloacetic acids (HAAs) have long underpinned DBP regulation, shaping monitoring and treatment strategies. However, recent analytical advances have fundamentally reshaped our understanding of DBPs. In this perspective, we examine how high-resolution mass spectrometry (HRMS)-based nontargeted analysis (NTA) has expanded the detectable DBP chemical space, while revealing key limitations that hinder translation from detection to identification. We then highlight emerging mass spectrometry and computational approaches as key pathways toward scalable DBP discovery and identification. We further examine the disconnect between rapid DBP discovery and limited toxicological understanding, highlighting key limitations of current toxicity assessments, including high-dose testing paradigms, fragmented end points, and overlooked mixture effects. To address these challenges, we propose an exposome-oriented framework as a conceptual model that integrates comprehensive chemical characterization with toxicity assessment, highlighting the need for future computational tools and prioritization strategies. Bridging chemical diversity to health relevance will be critical for prioritizing DBPs of concern and supporting risk-informed water quality management and public health protection.

Environmental Science & Technology.title: Investigations of New Particle Formation Mechanisms in North China Plain during the Spring Campaign Based on Observations and Simulations.
Environmental Science & Technology.abstract: New particle formation (NPF) plays a critical role in atmospheric aerosol loading, yet the mechanisms controlling NPF under high-pollution conditions remain poorly understood. Ground-based measurements and GEOS-Chem-APM simulations were combined to investigate the factors governing NPF in a typical industrial city over North China Plain. During the spring campaign (3 May-2 June 2016), 10 NPF days were identified, each preceded by nighttime northwesterly ventilation and occurring under dry daytime conditions. The model reproduced 6 of 10 observed NPF events, whereas the remaining 4 showed substantially weaker simulated nucleation. Well-simulated events were generally associated with low relative humidity (RH) and condensation sink (CS) environment. NH3 remained in large excess throughout the campaign. In our test, increasing H2SO4 by up to a factor of 3 substantially enhanced nucleation rate (J) but did not fully reproduce the observed particle evolution, while replacing modeled RH and aerosol surface area with observations only moderately adjusted J. The model underestimated growth rates by 51% and 75% on well-simulated and poorly simulated days. These results indicate that nighttime ventilation reduces surface area and CS of pre-existing aerosol loading, favoring NPF, while successful reproduction of observed NPF depends jointly on diverse precursor-driven nucleation, aerosol scavenging, and subsequent particle growth.

Environmental Science & Technology.title: Cross-Level Responses of Freshwater Zooplankton to Micro/Nanoplastics: A Meta-Analysis Integrating Individual- to Community-Level Evidence.
Environmental Science & Technology.abstract: Despite the known threats of micro/nanoplastics (MNPs) to freshwater ecosystems, their risks to zooplankton remain poorly resolved because existing evidence is fragmented across biological levels. Consequently, associations between lower-level responses and population- and community-level outcomes remain unclear. Here, we synthesized 3042 research cases from controlled experiments worldwide covering 12 response categories. We found significant overall negative effects of MNPs in systems without predators, with predators, and with predator-conditioned medium. Although molecular-level evidence remains limited, a consistent hierarchical response pattern emerged under predator-absent conditions. We therefore propose a conceptual hierarchical effect pathway (HEP) framework integrating effect sizes and cross-level associations. Within this framework, MNPs exposure was associated with increased ingestion of MNPs, physiological damage, feeding impairment, and reduced activity and defense. These responses formed an upstream tier associated with life-history impairments, including impaired growth and development, reduced reproductive capacity, and reduced survival, although these associations do not establish temporal ordering or causation. Under predator-present conditions, negative population- and community-level effects were also observed. Effect magnitudes also varied with MNPs characteristics, exposure duration, and zooplankton group. Together, the HEP framework clarifies cross-level associations and helps identify informative endpoints and incorporate food-web context into risk assessment of MNPs.

Environmental Science & Technology.title: Global Potential of No-Tillage in Enhancing Soil Carbon and Reducing Greenhouse Gas Emissions While Sustaining Crop Yields.
Environmental Science & Technology.abstract: Pursuing the balance between environmental sustainability and agricultural productivity remains a critical challenge for achieving global sustainable development goals. No-tillage (NT), as a key measure of sustainable conservation and climate-smart agriculture, offers a promising approach to addressing this challenge. However, its comprehensive effects on soil carbon accumulation, greenhouse gas emissions, and crop yields remain unquantified at the global scale, limiting our ability to optimize both environmental and agronomic outcomes. Here, we conducted such a global synthesis by combining a meta-analysis of 8,303 paired observations from 1,371 studies with a random forest model to assess the influence of site conditions and management on NT effects. Our meta-analysis demonstrates integrated benefits of NT in enhancing soil organic carbon (SOC) stocks in 0-30 cm layer by 11.0% and mitigating greenhouse gas (the sum of CO2, CH4, and N2O in CO2-equivalent) emissions by 13.5%, without a significant impact on crop yields (-0.6% ± 1.5%). The integrated benefits are stronger in drier climates and coarser-textured soils, and they exhibit significant time-dependent patterns. Our prediction identifies 44% of global croplands as being optimal for NT's integrated benefits, mainly in Africa, South Asia, and North America. Adopting NT in these areas would result in a 4.8% increase in major food-crop yields, a 15.2% increase in 0-30 cm SOC stocks, and a 6.4% reduction in global cropland emissions, respectively. These findings underscore the relevance of implementing NT in suitable regions by adopting it into Good Agricultural Practice Guidelines.

Environmental Science & Technology.title: Pollutant Release and Transfer Registers (PRTRs) as a Cornerstone of Global Chemicals Management: Current Gaps and Future Directions.
Environmental Science & Technology.abstract: Pollutant Release and Transfer Register (PRTR) systems in different countries are key tools for global chemicals management and an important data source for measuring progress toward achieving Sustainable Development Goal 12 of sustainable consumption and production patterns. However, current implementations face several structural and functional limitations that hinder the broad applicability of the PRTR reporting data. These limitations can be categorized into two main aspects: within-system issues and between-system inconsistencies. Within systems, data gaps can result from limited monitoring of nonpoint sources, incomplete reporting, exemptions due to thresholds and confidentiality agreements, and other similar factors, while data inaccuracies can be caused by estimation errors, duplicated counts, and other related issues. Between systems, differences in chemical lists, threshold settings, emission source types, reporting methods, and other discrepancies can hinder data comparability and integration, limiting the effectiveness of global chemicals management. Addressing these issues, through unified pollutant lists, harmonized reporting methodologies, expanded source coverage, and improved data verification, can significantly strengthen the utility of PRTR systems, advancing an integrated and evidence-based global sound management of chemicals.

Environmental Science & Technology.title: Fe(II) Speciation Regulates Microbial Metabolic Reprogramming and Phototrophic Fe(II) Mineralization in Rhodopseudomonas palustris SX2.
Environmental Science & Technology.abstract: Phototrophic iron mineralization (PIM) is a keystone biogeochemical process linking anoxic iron redox transformations to carbon sequestration. Although PIM is widely documented, how Fe(II) speciation impacts cell physiology and thus causes divergent mineralization phenotypes remains poorly understood. In this study, we systematically investigated the physiological, mineralogical, and molecular responses of a newly isolated photoferrotroph, Rhodopseudomonas palustris SX2, exposed to uncomplexed Fe(II) [Fe(II) without OM] versus organically complexed Fe(II) [Fe(II)-OM] under anoxic and illuminated conditions. We demonstrate that distinct Fe(II) speciation drives divergent metabolic reprogramming for rapid metabolic adaptation and phototrophic biomineralization phenotypes. Fe(II) without OM triggered cell-surface encrustation and activated stress-mitigation and metal-efflux systems, whereas Fe(II)-OM stimulated the formation of discrete intracellular iron nanoparticles while upregulating photosynthetic light harvesting and autotrophic CO2 fixation. Furthermore, genetic knockout and complementation confirmed that the pioABC operon constitutes the indispensable electron conduit driving Fe(II) oxidation across both speciation regimes, with organic complexation significantly enhancing its transcriptional activation. Our findings reveal how metabolic adaptation driven by Fe(II) speciation dictates the spatial distribution of biogenic iron minerals and regulates the efficiency of coupled carbon sequestration in anoxic ecosystems.

Environmental Science & Technology.title: Wastewater Treatment Plants as Anchor Infrastructure for Geothermal Energy in Cold Regions.
Environmental Science & Technology.abstract: Thermal constraints in cold regions suppress biological treatment, increase energy demand, and elevate greenhouse gas emissions of existing wastewater treatment plants (WWTPs), and remain a major barrier to the deployment of adequate sanitation infrastructure in many cold-region communities. Where geothermal resources exist, low-enthalpy hydrothermal heat is well matched to this energy gap. Yet, WWTPs are underrecognized anchors for broader geothermal deployment, providing a continuous, weather-independent thermal offtake through which subsurface CAPEX can be amortized. We reframe geothermal-WWTP integration as a system-level enabler that benefits both parts. Using three cascaded configurations for a full-scale WWTP, a rapid techno-economic analysis identifies three trends: energy and carbon savings/revenues alone are insufficient under realistic policy stacks, whereas crediting the upgrade-deferral value of geothermally enhanced treatment makes the project economically favorable across most policy scenarios. Globally, this triple intersection encompasses ∼11,600 catalogued WWTPs serving ∼280 million people, with a further estimate of ∼48 million people in the same regions beyond current service radii. The opportunity is greatest in cold, remote, and underserved communities, where local geothermal resources, treatment intensification, and community-scale demand together carry a case that no single driver could sustain alone.

Environmental Science & Technology.title: Multi-Omics Gut Microbiome Species Communities and Functional Modules Linking Metal Exposures to Children's Neurodevelopmental Health in a Canadian Birth Cohort.
Environmental Science & Technology.abstract: Early life metal exposure has been associated with adverse neurodevelopment, with gut microbiome disruption proposed as a potential pathway. However, most studies have focused on individual taxa or pathways, despite microbes functioning within ecological communities and coordinated functional networks. Here, we integrated stool metal measurements, shotgun metagenomics, metatranscriptomics, and neurodevelopmental assessments in 116 children aged 8-12 years from the GESTE birth cohort in Sherbrooke, Canada. Nineteen metals were quantified in stool samples, and neurodevelopment was assessed using parent-reported behavioral scales, attention performance testing, and resting-state fMRI. Using network-based community detection, we identified 10 co-occurring species communities (SCs) from metagenomic data and 16 coexpressed functional modules (FMs) from metatranscriptomic data and evaluated their associations with metal exposures and neurodevelopmental outcomes. Higher levels of lead, cadmium, aluminum, zinc, copper, and magnesium were associated with lower abundance of Streptococcus- and Veillonella-dominated SCs, while multiple metals were associated with lower abundance of amino acid metabolism and carbohydrate degradation FMs. Exploratory mediation analyses suggested potential indirect associations between stool metals and parent-reported ADHD-related traits througha methionine cycle-related FM or sequentially through a Clostridium spp. SC and a Factor 420 biosynthesis FM. These findings suggest that stool metal concentrations are associated with community-level variations in gut microbial composition and function, some of which were further associated with parent-reported ADHD-related traits.

Environmental Science & Technology.title: Size- and Time-Resolved Emission Rates of Particulate Matter Mass, Chemical Constituents, and Oxidative Potential from Indoor Sources.
Environmental Science & Technology.abstract: We quantified the time- and size-resolved emission rates of particulate matter (PM) mass, its chemical constituents, and OP (via dithiothreitol assay) from six indoor sources in a test chamber (two types of incense, candle, toaster, humidifier, and cigarette). Both the chemical composition and mass-normalized OP (OPm) varied little temporally. However, both the chemical composition and OPm varied with particle size from <0.25 to 10 μm, with quasi-ultrafine particles (Q-UFPs < 0.25 μm) showing the highest OPm. The particle size distribution of the PM emitted from these sources was mostly unimodal, with both PM10 mass and OP emission rate concentrated in the Q-UFP size range. Given the abundance of Q-UFPs in the emitted PM with their high intrinsic OP, we find that 37 ± 3% of the emitted PM10 mass and OP from these sources has the potential to deposit in the respiratory tract, 45 ± 2% of which deposits in the alveolar region. An exploratory exposure assessment suggests that for an equal dose of PM10 mass and OP originating from these indoor sources vs ambient PM, the emissions from the tested indoor sources will likely result in a 76 ± 10% higher dose of alveolar-deposited mass and OP. Collectively, these results emphasize the need to better quantify the size-resolved toxicological properties of PM from myriad indoor emission sources to reliably estimate the resulting health risks.

Environmental Science & Technology.title: Assessing 50 Years of Salt Effects in Heterogeneous Photocatalysis.
Environmental Science & Technology.abstract: Heterogeneous photocatalysis has been studied for the treatment of recalcitrant compounds for half a century, but one of the severe limitations for practical oxidation treatment continues to be the inhibitory effect of salt found in real water matrices. The negative impact of Na+, K+, Cl-, and other ionic species is rarely quantified, as there has been no systematic way to discuss salt effects, making the evaluation of photocatalysis performance across studies difficult and imprecise. In analyzing 50 years of literature for this review, we identified >1,200 publications on heterogeneous photocatalysis in different water types, such as seawater, brackish water, and industrial brines. Just 84 studies reported degradation rates in deionized and salt-containing water, with nearly all involving TiO2 as the photocatalyst composition and charged dye compounds as the model contaminant class. To analyze the kinetic data extracted from these studies, we introduce the photocatalysis salt-effect (PSE) metric as calculated through the relative salt-effectiveness evaluation (RSEE) method, quantifying the percent change in degradation rate when the water matrix contains a salt species. We identified an unexpected correlation between PSE and ionic strength (IS), irrespective of the contaminant, at solution pH values less than the TiO2 point-of-zero-charge (PZC), which is the plausible result of salt-induced particle aggregation at high ionic strengths during photocatalyst testing. While most published results showed salt inhibition of photocatalysis (-100% < PSE < -5%), there is evidence for salt promotion (PSE > +5%) and salt tolerance (-5% < PSE < +5%), which challenges the notion that salinity is always detrimental to photocatalytic activity. These findings highlight the opportunity to study fully and systematically the relationships among contaminant structure, photocatalyst PZC, solution pH, IS, and salt type. The PSE-based framework would be critical in understanding the effects of more complex water matrices and in ultimately developing salt-tolerant and salt-promoted heterogeneous photocatalysis for practical water treatment.

Environmental Science & Technology.title: Mild Oxidant Regulation of *H Coverage Promotes Electrocatalytic Nitrate Reduction to N2 in Low-Conductivity Media.
Environmental Science & Technology.abstract: Electrocatalytic nitrate reduction reaction (NO3RR) has attracted growing interest for converting nitrate (NO3-) into ammonium (NH4+), yet NH4+ production from dilute, low-conductivity waters is constrained by high energy consumption, limited NO3- availability, and costly product recovery. Steering NO3RR directly toward benign N2 therefore represents a more practical route, but this pathway is often suppressed by excessive surface *H coverage, which drives the overhydrogenation of nitrogen intermediates to NH4+. Here, we report a mild oxidant-assisted coelectrolysis strategy that regulates interfacial *H coverage and promotes NO3--to-N2 conversion in a Cu nanoparticle-decorated Ni cathode membrane electrochemical reactor. This reactor separates a highly conductive electrochemical chamber from a NO3--containing chemical chamber, enabling NO3- reduction in low-conductivity media while maintaining a less negative cathodic potential. Mild oxidants, including H2O2, O2, CH3COOOH, and KIO4, consumed excess *H and redirected the reaction pathway toward N-N coupling. With H2O2 as a representative oxidant, N2 selectivity increased from 13.47% without H2O2 to 87.25% at 100 mM H2O2. Mechanistic analyses revealed that H2O2 decreases interfacial *H abundance, which suppresses NH4+ formation and facilitates the dimerization of nitrogen-containing intermediates. Verification in real low-conductivity groundwater further supports this strategy as a mechanistic basis for designing selective, low-energy electrochemical denitrification systems for low-conductivity NO3--contaminated media.

Environmental Science & Technology.title: Waste as Feedstock, Electrolyte, and Target: Closing the Loop in Electrochemical H2O2 Water Treatment.
Environmental Science & Technology.abstract: Electrochemical H2O2 production is increasingly positioned as an on-site route for water oxidation, disinfection, and resource recovery. However, its environmental translation remains constrained by a basic design mismatch between catalyst development in clean electrolytes and deployment in chemically variable waste streams. This Perspective argues that progress should move beyond catalyst-centered performance metrics toward a closed-loop, waste-centered framework. The key issue is not how to isolate H2O2 electrosynthesis from wastewater complexity but when and how that complexity can be engineered. Solid and liquid waste streams can provide carbon, heteroatoms, and metals for impurity-resilient electrodes. Meanwhile, wastewater constituents can regulate interfacial ion distribution, water structure, oxygen transport, proton availability, intermediate stabilization, and side reactions. Electrogenerated H2O2 can be routed to contaminant transformation, disinfection, detoxification, and metal recovery. We discuss design principles for converting heterogeneous waste feedstocks into catalytic interfaces, defining wastewater operating windows, matching reactor architectures with real water matrices, and evaluating circularity through life-cycle and techno-economic accounting. We identify critical benchmarks─matrix descriptors, durability mechanisms, byproduct control, reactor-treatment matching, and transparent environmental safeguards─needed to turn circular H2O2 concepts into verifiable water-treatment technologies.

Environmental Science & Technology.title: Light-Induced Formation of Volatile Organic Compounds from Bleach Cleaning in Indoor Environments.
Environmental Science & Technology.abstract: Surface bleach cleaning is a common indoor activity that releases abundant strong oxidants, including hypochlorous acid (HOCl) and chlorine gas (Cl2), which can significantly influence indoor chemistry. While bleach-driven chemical transformations are recognized, the specific role of illumination remains poorly understood. This study combines field measurements and laboratory flow tube experiments to investigate volatile organic compound (VOC) formation from reactions between bleach emissions and surface-sorbed species, e.g., kitchen-derived organic films, under illuminated conditions. In real-world indoor settings, we observed that bleach cleaning under light predominantly generates oxygenated VOCs (OVOCs), accounting for ∼92% of total emissions. Saturated carbonyls contributed the most (∼82%), such as C6H12O, C9H18O, and C2H4O. Flow tube experiments using surrogate compounds and kitchen-collected surface films confirmed that OVOCs are generated via heterogeneous reactions between surface-bound organics (e.g., fatty acids, amides, amino acids) and radicals produced from photolysis of bleach-derived oxidants. VOC production was found to depend on surface accumulation and aging, with more accumulated and aged surfaces producing greater quantities and more diverse products. These findings provide important insights into VOC production from indoor surface chemistry initiated by bleach cleaning under typical indoor lighting conditions, advancing our understanding of volatile byproduct formation from indoor bleach photochemistry.

Environmental Science & Technology.title: Ammonia Triggers Interfacial Breakpoint Chlorination to Enhance Micropollutant Degradation and Reshapes Chlorinated Byproduct Formation during Electrochlorination.
Environmental Science & Technology.abstract: Electrochlorination is a promising technology for micropollutant degradation in decentralized water treatment. However, ammonia can alter chlorine chemistry. This study investigates the effect of ammonia on micropollutant degradation and chlorinated byproduct formation during electrochlorination using the RuO2/IrO2-Ti anode. Compared to electrochlorination at 10 mM chloride without ammonia, the presence of 1 mM ammonia increased the degradation rate constants of metronidazole and carbamazepine by 2.7- and 4.5-fold, respectively. This enhancement is consistent with interfacial breakpoint chlorination, defined as preferential chlorine-ammonia conversion within an anode-adjacent, chlorine-rich aqueous diffusion layer before complete bulk mixing. During electrochlorination with ammonia, dissolved HO• contributed to micropollutant degradation. Electron paramagnetic resonance provided qualitative evidence of HO• formation, whereas nitrobenzene was used as a probe to quantify its steady-state concentration. The ammonia-induced steady-state HO• concentration reached 2.4 × 10-13 M at 1 mM ammonia, whereas the HO• contribution was negligible without ammonia. Meanwhile, 1-5 mM ammonia reduced the total yields of chlorinated byproducts by only 25-31% during electrochlorination. The limited suppression is consistent with concurrent competition between ammonia and dissolved organic matter for locally generated chlorine within the anode-adjacent region. These findings identify near-anode chlorine-ammonia conversion as a route to reactive-species formation and micropollutant degradation, while showing that chlorinated byproducts remain a concern in ammonia-containing electrochlorination systems.

Environmental Science & Technology.title: Source or Sink: Bioanalytical and Chemical Profiling of New and Field-Weathered Plastics.
Environmental Science & Technology.abstract: Plastics contain complex mixtures of chemicals that can leach into the aquatic environment. Conversely, the high sorption capacity of certain polymers renders plastics passive samplers for environmental pollutants from ambient waters. We evaluated whether effects from chemicals that are extractable or leachable from plastics from the North Pacific Ocean are dominated by plastic-associated or sorbed environmental compounds. First, bioanalytical profiling of chemical mixtures from solvent extracts of field-weathered marine plastics in cell-based bioassays was compared to that of chemicals from solvent extracts of newly purchased counterparts of the field plastics. Second, the new plastics were artificially UV-weathered and solvent-extracted, and the leachate waters were enriched with solid-phase extraction and dosed into a test battery of four in vitro bioassays where activation of the arylhydrocarbon receptor, oxidative stress response, and/or cytotoxicity were most responsive. Finally, chemical screening was performed using high-resolution mass spectrometry with subsequent mixture effect modeling to identify toxicity drivers. The results showed a multifaceted picture: Newly purchased high-durability outdoor products caused higher effects before weathering, whereas food packaging tended to show increased effects after field weathering. The analyzed chemicals could partially explain the observed effects (<0.1-98%). Our study underlines the relevance of field weathering for marine plastics and their potential to leach chemicals of concern into the environment.

Environmental Science & Technology.title: Molecular Interactions between Styrene Oligomers and Human Serum Albumin: A Multiscale Computational Study of a Plastic-Derived Environmental Contaminant.
Environmental Science & Technology.abstract: Micro- and nanoplastics are pervasive environmental pollutants known to accumulate in human organs. While the hazards of larger plastic particles are under intense investigation, the toxicological impact of molecular-level plastic oligomers with dimensions around 1 nm is a critical and underexplored area. This study provides a comprehensive molecular-level in silico characterization of the binding interactions between styrene oligomers (1-7 units) and HSA, characterizing their molecular basis and its potential relevance to HSA's ligand transport function. A multilevel computational approach was employed, integrating molecular docking, MD simulations, DFT, MM/PBSA binding free energy calculations, and ProLIF interaction fingerprinting. FA1 accommodated 82-95% of the most favorable docking poses for oligomers containing three to seven styrene units and exhibited the lowest docking scores, reaching -11.9 kcal·mol-1, compared with -6.4 kcal·mol-1 for the monomer. MD simulations confirmed the structural stability of oligomer-HSA complexes, further supported by dynamic cross-correlation, principal component, and solvent-accessible surface area analyses. Quantum biochemistry analyses further confirmed FA1 as the most energetically favorable binding pocket, with an average interaction energy of -117.47 kcal·mol-1 compared with -73.96 kcal·mol-1 for FA6, a hierarchy independently reproduced by MM/PBSA calculations (R = 0.82). For the hexamer and heptamer, FA1 exhibited energetic advantages of 27.39 and 21.84 kcal·mol-1, respectively. These findings indicate that HSA binds styrene oligomers with high stability and affinity at FA1, providing a molecular basis for further investigation of their potential relevance to ligand transport and systemic exposure to plastic-derived contaminants.

Environmental Science & Technology.title: Interfacial Triplet-Energy Funneling Directs Energy-Transfer-Mediated Singlet Oxygen Generation for Deep Toluene Mineralization.
Environmental Science & Technology.abstract: Photocatalytic oxidation is a promising strategy for volatile organic compounds (VOCs) abatement, but incomplete mineralization and carbonaceous intermediate accumulation remain major challenges, especially when conventional charge-transfer pathways generate nonselective radical reactive oxygen species. Selective activation of molecular oxygen toward singlet oxygen (1O2) offers a potential route to controlled oxidation, yet efficient energy-transfer-mediated 1O2 generation in solid-state photocatalysts remains difficult to achieve. Herein, a strongly coupled In(OH)3/ZnGa2O4 heterojunction with an electronic structure consistent with an S-scheme configuration is constructed to investigate interfacial excited-state regulation. Spectroscopic measurements indicate modified excited-state relaxation and a reduced effective singlet-triplet energy separation, which may favor singlet-to-triplet conversion. Combined spectroscopic analyses, quenching experiments, and density functional theory calculations support a proposed interfacial triplet-energy-funneling pathway involving ZnGa2O4-related/interfacial triplet-related states and subsequent energy transfer to adsorbed O2 for 1O2 generation. As a result, the optimized In(OH)3/ZnGa2O4 photocatalyst achieves 98.3% toluene removal and 92.4% mineralization in a continuous-flow gas-phase reactor, together with excellent cycling stability and humidity tolerance. Mechanistic results further suggest that a pathway involving 1O2 contributes to methyl oxidation and the subsequent conversion of oxygenated intermediates, potentially limiting carbonaceous residue accumulation. This work provides an excited-state-engineering strategy for selective molecular oxygen activation and offers a promising route toward efficient, durable, and deeply mineralizing photocatalytic VOCs abatement.

Environmental Science & Technology.title: Suppressing Proton Affinity of Surface Oxygen for Enhanced N2 Selectivity in Mn-Based NH3-SCR Catalysts.
Environmental Science & Technology.abstract: Inferior N2 selectivity remains a critical challenge for Mn-based catalysts in NH3-SCR denitration. Here, using atomically dispersed Mn on anatase (Mn1/TiO2) and MnO2 as model catalysts, we elucidate the origin of surface oxygen activity and the role of surface oxygen in the formation of N2O. Both catalysts achieved >99% NO conversion in the temperature range of 175-300 °C (WHSV = 60,000 mL·g-1·h-1). Compared with the poor selectivity of α-MnO2 (1.2% at 300 °C), Mn1/TiO2 maintained >88.0% N2 selectivity in 50-300 °C. Density functional theory calculations revealed that the high affinity of surface oxygen for protons results in overoxidation of NH3-derived intermediates, thus promoting N2O formation. Orbital interaction analysis manifested that surface oxygen activity in octahedrally coordinated catalysts depends on the spin polarization in transition-metal 3d bands. Atomic dispersion of Mn sites on oxides with nonspin-polarized dxy orbitals was demonstrated as a universal strategy to boost N2 selectivity. This work deepens the fundamental understanding of surface oxygen activity in catalysts, paving a way for designing Mn-based catalysts with excellent N2 selectivity.

Environmental Science & Technology.title: Coal Tar-Based Driveway Sealant Extract Induces Mutations in Liver, Bone Marrow, and Germ Cells of MutaMouse Male Mice.
Environmental Science & Technology.abstract: Coal tar-based driveway sealants (CTS) are a widespread but underrecognized source of human exposure to mutagenic polycyclic aromatic hydrocarbons (PAHs). We used Duplex Sequencing, an error-corrected sequencing technology, to assess the mutagenicity of a complex PAH mixture extracted from a CTS in MutaMouse male mice. We observed significant dose-dependent increases in mutation frequency (MF) in liver and bone marrow, with mutation spectra dominated by C:G > A:T substitutions, closely resembling a mutational signature linked to human cancers associated with tobacco smoking. In germ cells, we did not observe a statistically significant increase in MF, although there was a positive dose-response trend and enrichment of C:G > A:T mutations at higher doses. The mutagenic effects of CTS in germ cells were supported by a statistically significant increase in mutant frequency measured using the plaque-based lacZ assay. Tissue-specific analyses revealed greater mutation susceptibility and potency in liver, likely reflecting its central role in PAH metabolism. Mutation spectrum analysis showed that the mutagenic profile of the CTS extract largely resembled that of benzo(a)pyrene; however, detailed spectral analysis indicated additional contributions from other PAHs or PAH metabolites that produced distinct mutational patterns. Collectively, our findings demonstrate that the CTS extract induces tissue-specific mutagenic responses driven by characteristic C:G > A:T mutations, offering mechanistic insight into how environmental PAH mixtures contribute to mutation burden and cancer risk.

Environmental Science & Technology.title: Market-Average Data Can Misrepresent Supply Chain Environmental Impacts and Their Uncertainty.
Environmental Science & Technology.abstract: Market-average data sets are often used in life cycle assessment and carbon accounting when the production route of a procured good is unknown. The uncertainty this introduces is commonly characterized using generic pedigree matrix factors, which do not reflect how variability across production geographies and technologies differs between goods. Here, we develop a hybrid method that combines pedigree matrix uncertainty characterization within individual production routes with market-share-weighted Monte Carlo sampling between known production routes to represent uncertainty about which route supplied the good. We compare it with conventional market-average uncertainty analysis for 30 economically important goods. For climate impacts, conventional 5th-95th interpercentile intervals are narrower than route-weighted sampling intervals for 25 goods, at least 50% narrower for 14 goods, and up to 82% narrower. Conventional intervals exclude the central climate impact estimates of 44% of possible production routes. Route-weighted sampling captures these outcomes and reveals multimodality and impact-category-specific uncertainty profiles that conventional analysis does not. Variance decomposition distinguishes geographical and technological differences between routes from uncertainty within routes, helping prioritize supplier data collection. These differences show that conventional uncertainty estimates can mislead and may not capture how substantially initial estimates could change when supplier-specific data become available.

Environmental Science & Technology.title: Carbon Source Diversity Shapes DOM Chemodiversity and Antibiotic Resistome in Earthworm Casts.
Environmental Science & Technology.abstract: The earthworm gut acts as a hotspot for reprocessing ingested organic matter, thereby altering carbon availability. These changes reshape microbial communities and competitive interactions, potentially affecting the dissemination of antibiotic resistance genes (ARGs) in the gut. Beyond substrate amount, substrate diversity shapes these processes, yet its role remains unknown. We established microcosm experiments with a substrate-diversity gradient, combining FT-ICR MS and metagenomics to investigate dissolved organic matter (DOM) chemistry, microbial traits and ARGs in earthworm guts. Higher substrate diversity enriched carbon-centered metabolic genes and increased gut DOM availability, possibly through the proliferation of polysaccharide-degrading microorganisms with larger genomes. However, higher carbon availability may have increased microbial nutrient demand, accompanied by reductions in CHON-containing compounds and stronger microbial competition. ARG enrichment was associated with greater potential for microbial competition, as indicated by stronger negative microbial interactions and higher competition indices derived from genome scale metabolic models. In vitro monoculture of gut-derived pathogenic Klebsiella pneumoniae showed that substrate diversity enriched multidrug- and β-lactam-resistance genes and reshaped the resistome. Collectively, these findings suggest that increased substrate diversity modifies earthworm-driven carbon reprocessing, may reshape microbial resource competition and promote ARG enrichment, providing insights into the linkage between organic matter processing and resistome in soil fauna.

Environmental Science & Technology.title: Implementation Gap in Global Power Capacity Expansion to meet Paris Agreement Climate Targets.
Environmental Science & Technology.abstract: Meeting the Paris Agreement's climate targets demands an unprecedented expansion of renewable energy. Despite global commitments, significant implementation gaps persist due to economic, policy, and technical uncertainties. Here, we develop a Global Power Capacity Dynamics Framework, integrating facility-level data, machine learning and transition modeling to assess the feasibility of global power expansion. Analyzing 215,849 power plant units across five status modes (operating, planned, canceled, standby, retired), the framework explicitly incorporates the likelihood of planned capacity realization and the conversion of existing fossil assets. We find that by 2030, only 51% [40%-61%] of announced planned capacity is expected to become operational, while 26% [19%-36%] is likely to be canceled, with fossil fuel projects, especially coal, facing a cancellation rate of about 35%. Global operational capacity is projected to reach 9727 GW [9626-9848], including 178 GW [159-198] of existing fossil units requiring conversion or replacement (e.g., coal-to-gas, fossil-to-biomass). Although renewables dominate the planned pipeline, they are projected to constitute only 52% of the global energy mix by 2030, well below levels needed to meet climate goals. Regional disparities are pronounced: Asia, despite its relatively low cancellation rate, faces the world's largest implementation gap, requiring an additional 2488 GW of solar and contending with 523 GW of stranded coal capacity to remain on a 1.5 °C pathway. This study provides the first probabilistic, facility-level assessment of global power capacity trajectories, revealing critical shortfalls in planned deployment and underscoring the urgency of aligning capacity expansion with climate targets.

Environmental Science & Technology.title: Environmental Mechanochemistry: From Force-Induced Reactivity to Aqueous Reaction Platforms.
Environmental Science & Technology.abstract: Mechanochemistry is increasingly used in environmental research, but is still commonly treated as a material synthesis or pretreatment step rather than a mode of driving reactions that directly affects pathways relevant to pollution control and resource recovery. This Perspective argues that its environmental significance is most evident when force not only changes material properties before use, but also alters how reactions proceed during operation. We compare how force becomes chemically effective in inorganic and organic systems and classify environmental applications according to its primary role. Using zerovalent iron (ZVI) as a representative example, we show that mechanochemistry can simultaneously alleviate multiple bottlenecks in ZVI preparation, storage, and application. Earlier studies have shown that force can regulate ZVI lattice structure, surface state, and interfacial charge transfer. The wet-milling mechanochemical reactor (MCR) extends these effects into aqueous operation by applying force during rather than before reaction. This intensifies solid-liquid contact, accelerates heterogeneous kinetics, and, in some systems, shifts target transformation from surface-confined pathways toward subsurface redistribution and lattice-associated capture. Future advances should identify systems in which force can strengthen reactions sufficiently to open pathways that conventional treatment processes do not readily access.

Environmental Science & Technology.title: Mitochondrial-Endocrine Axis Dysfunction Mediates Diet-Dependent Susceptibility to Nanoplastic Ovarian Toxicity and PCOS Risk.
Environmental Science & Technology.abstract: Nanoplastics (NPs) pollution represents an emerging threat to reproductive health, yet how dietary habits modulate this toxicity remains largely unexplored. Here, mice were assigned to a control (CD), high-fat (HFD), or high-fiber (HFib) diet and received oral doses of deuterated polystyrene nanoparticles at 0, 5, or 25 mg/kg/day over an eight-week period. Ovarian NP accumulation was dose-dependent under CD, reaching 23.33 ± 5.39 μg/g tissue at the highest dose. HFD markedly elevated this burden to 96.87 ± 13.44 μg/g, whereas HFib significantly reduced it to 7.77 ± 1.32 μg/g. Functionally, HFD synergized with NPs to disrupt estrous cyclicity (only 13% regular cycles), suppress anti-Müllerian hormone by 74%, and increase follicular atresia rate, while HFib maintained near-normal ovarian physiology. Transcriptomics identified steroid hormone biosynthesis and oxidative phosphorylation (OXPHOS) as core pathways convergently dysregulated by NPs across all diets. Mechanistically, HFD amplified NP-induced ovarian oxidative stress, inflammation, and mitochondrial OXPHOS impairment, culminating in hyperandrogenism and profound estradiol deficiency. Conversely, HFib preserved aromatase expression and mitochondrial respiratory capacity, thereby restoring steroidogenic homeostasis. Mendelian randomization further linked human orthologues of these dysregulated genes, including UQCR10 and COX4I1 encoding mitochondrial complex III and IV subunits, to elevated polycystic ovary syndrome (PCOS) risk, highlighting the central role of OXPHOS disruption. These findings establish a diet-NP interaction pattern with implications for reproductive health guidance in populations.

Environmental Science & Technology.title: Why Phytate Persists: Mechanisms of Exceptional Binding and Stability on Soil Mineral Surfaces.
Environmental Science & Technology.abstract: Phytate, a six-phosphate compound that stores plant phosphorus, is a stable component of soil phosphorus, yet mechanisms underlying its persistence remain unclear. Here, we combined adsorption experiments, spectroscopy, X-ray scattering, and molecular modeling to investigate phytate interactions with five soil minerals: goethite, hematite, quartz, montmorillonite, and kaolinite. Iron oxides exhibited up to 5-fold greater adsorption capacities than quartz and clays. Natural organic matter caused negligible desorption of mineral-bound phytate, whereas phytate displaced adsorbed natural organic matter, demonstrating competitive and stable phytate-mineral associations. Adsorption capacities normalized to orthophosphate binding-site densities implied multiphosphate coordination for phytate on iron oxides, but binding beyond nominal orthophosphate sites on montmorillonite. Molecular dynamics simulations captured one to three phosphate groups in phytate associations with iron oxides; metal cation screening of electrostatic repulsion facilitated binding on negatively charged quartz and montmorillonite. Infrared spectroscopy revealed coupled vibrational responses of phosphate and inositol ring moieties on goethite, but primarily phosphate responses on montmorillonite. X-ray total scattering determined a feature at 2.7 Å, supporting inner-sphere coordination on iron oxides and consistent with quantum mechanics-based energy calculations, whereas quartz and clay features indicated interfacial reorganization. These findings establish mineral-specific mechanisms of phytate stabilization, with implications for persistence and bioavailability in soils.

Environmental Science & Technology.title: Targeted Coupling of Electrogenerated Reactive Oxygen Species for Deep Pollutant Mineralization.
Environmental Science & Technology.abstract: Electrochemical oxidation technology holds great promise for wastewater treatment. However, the inherent limitations of single-component reactive oxygen species (ROS) and their low yield impede thorough mineralization of organic pollutants and elevate energy consumption. Herein, we develop a directed ROS coupling oxidation (DRCO) system, which employs a Ni-Sb-SnO2 anode that leverages Ni(III)/Ni(II) redox cycling for highly selective OH generation, coupled with a CrMn@C anode for 1O2 production, significantly enhancing the coexisting ROS yield. By leveraging the electron-withdrawing and donating synergistic effect of •OH and 1O2, the DRCO system removes 61.2-78.5% total organic carbon (TOC) for diverse organics within 20 min. The observed kinetic constants are 1.4-52.6 times higher than those of systems that use •OH or 1O2 alone. Furthermore, the DRCO system achieves 85.4% TOC removal for actual pharmaceutical wastewater and sustains operational stability over a 120 h continuous flow period. Compared to commercial anodes, the DRCO system reduces energy consumption by 72% (to 12.02 kW·h·kgTOC-1) while effectively suppressing the accumulation of toxic intermediate products. This work demonstrates that high-selectivity •OH generation and the elucidated dual-ROS synergistic mechanism jointly offer a viable strategy toward efficient and energy-conscious electrochemical water purification.

Environmental Science & Technology.title: Recovering Rare Earth Elements from Mining Effluent via Synergistic Angstrom-Scale Confinement and Phosphate-Mediated Coordination in MXene Membranes.
Environmental Science & Technology.abstract: Recovering rare earth elements (REEs) from complex aqueous streams is essential for advancing sustainable resource recovery but remains hindered by low REE concentrations and strong competition with impurity ions. Herein, we introduce a biomimetic MXene membrane that integrates phosphate-based molecular recognition with angstrom-level control of interlayer spacing to achieve the selective and continuous recovery of REEs from wastewaters. By intercalating aminophosphonic molecules within Ti3C2Tx layers, the membrane precisely tunes the nanochannel size and establishes coordinatively active oxygen sites that preferentially bind trivalent lanthanides under nanoconfinement. Such a design enables a synergistic mechanism in which steric exclusion and ligand-metal coordination coregulate ion transport, leading to markedly improved selectivity toward REE recovery. The optimized 2-AEP-M membrane exhibited a Ca2+/Dy3+ selectivity of 243.47 in simulated solutions and 130.69 in actual REE mining wastewater. After membrane separation and subsequent precipitation and calcination, REEs constituted 90.2% of the quantified cationic species in the recovered solid products. Experimental and computational analyses reveal that phosphate groups promote Dy3+ coordination, underpinning the observed ion discrimination. The membrane also demonstrates antiswelling stability and antibacterial properties, supporting its potential for long-term deployment. This work integrates chemical affinity with angstrom-confined transport, offering a platform for precise ion separation and sustainable REE recovery.

Environmental Science & Technology.title: Biogeochemical Control Points for Mitigating Metal(loid) Risk in Rice under Global Change.
Environmental Science & Technology.abstract: The uptake of arsenic (As), cadmium (Cd), and mercury (Hg) in rice is a global health concern. The variable biogeochemical processes that govern contamination risk, along with increased anthropogenic pressures, present significant obstacles to implementing mitigation strategies. This perspective highlights the biogeochemical processes governing the mobility and rice uptake of metal(loid)s across the soil-rice continuum and provides recent insights into mitigation strategies. An overview of anthropogenic stressors that may further exacerbate rice contamination, particularly climate change, is also provided. Finally, in the context of historical knowledge, we identify and discuss a future roadmap for research priorities and mitigation strategies, including (1) addressing variability in soil-rice systems that alters metal(loid) uptake dynamics, (2) investigating practical applications and mitigation strategies for farmers, and (3) expanding research into the myriad effects climate change may have on metal(loid) cycling.

Environmental Science & Technology.title: Mechanistic Insights into Humic Acid-Mediated Photosensitized Activation of Mn(VII) under UVA Irradiation.
Environmental Science & Technology.abstract: Ultraviolet A/permanganate [UVA/Mn(VII)] is a promising advanced oxidation process (AOP), while few studies have noticed that humic acid (HA) could enhance microcontaminant degradation in the process. For the first time, the promotive effect of HA and the underlying mechanisms were investigated in UVA/Mn(VII). HA significantly enhanced the generation of hydroxyl radical (HO•) and reactive manganese species (RMnS). Consequently, the pseudo-first-order reaction rate constants for microcontaminant degradation in UVA/Mn(VII)/HA were several to tens of times those in UVA/Mn(VII). The promotive effect of HA was attributed to the enhanced Mn(VII) activation by photogenerated reactive intermediates derived from irradiated HA. Among them, the excited triplet state of HA (3HA*) played a major role, which was also supported by benzophenone (BP), a model triplet state photosensitizer. The second-order reaction rate constants of Mn(VII) with 3HA* and 3BP* were determined to be 2.54(±0.31) × 108 and 2.88(±0.10) × 109 M-1 s-1, respectively. Spectroscopic analysis and theoretical calculations supported an electron transfer mechanism for the reactions of Mn(VII) with 3HA* and 3BP*. Mn(VII) accepted one electron from 3HA*/3BP* and was reduced to Mn(VI), which underwent disproportionation to form Mn(VII) and Mn(V), followed by HO• and other RMnS generation. These findings provide novel perspectives for the application of UVA/Mn(VII) in practical water treatment.

Environmental Science & Technology.title: Constructing Prospective Multiregional Input-Output Tables via Scenario-Constrained Optimization for Future Environmental Footprint Assessment.
Environmental Science & Technology.abstract: Prospective multiregional input-output (MRIO) tables that integrate scenarios from integrated assessment models (IAMs) support forward-looking environmental footprint analysis, but the trade-off between historical structural fidelity and scenario compliance has not been quantified. We constructed 12 prospective MRIO tables from EXIOBASE 2019 and the IMAGE SSP2 scenario for 2035, including a Leontief-based projection and 11 optimization-based projections under different combinations of scenario constraints on GDP, value added, sector outputs, as well as energy and agriculture consumption. Among the constraints, those on energy and agriculture consumption were satisfied at the highest cost in coefficient deviations from the Leontief-based projection and shifted the corresponding transaction flows most significantly. Regional shares of the global carbon footprint remained stable, but sectoral attribution within each region was substantially reshuffled, and the identification of high-growth consumption hotspots was sensitive to scenario compliance level. Some hotspots persisted at all levels of compliance. The consumption-based carbon footprint driven by China's final energy demand grew the fastest and emerged as a major new hotspot in 2035. The footprint of livestock consumption showed persistent high growth in multiple regions and India and the Rest of Asia rose in environmental significance through their industrial sectors.

Environmental Science & Technology.title: Global Steel Decarbonization under Policy, Technology, and Resource Constraints: A Process-Unit Agent-Based Model.
Environmental Science & Technology.abstract: Deep decarbonization of steel requires low-emission technologies to be deployed through a long-lived and heterogeneous asset fleet without disrupting steel supply. We developed a country-resolved agent-based model that follows global steel process units annually from 2023 to 2060. Units choose among continued operation, renewal, retrofit, conversion, retirement, and new construction, subject to construction time, linked upstream capacity, national production pathways, and annual supplies of scrap, hydrogen, natural gas, and pellets. Four scenarios distinguish stronger climate policy from improved technology and resource availability. Global process-chain CO2 emissions decline by 67-79% by 2060, reaching 0.476-0.737 Gt. The integrated case achieves the lowest emissions, but the two-component interventions do not independently outperform the reference case. Stronger policy changes when assets enter a finite transition queue, whereas technology and material conditions determine whether replacement routes can be built and operated at that time. By 2060, Scrap-EAF supplies 74-80% of crude steel, but residual unabated blast furnaces and coal-based direct reduction keep national steel pathways above their allocated levels in many countries. Deep decarbonization, therefore, depends on coordinating asset turnover, construction, and complementary material systems, rather than on technology availability or carbon-price pressure alone.

Environmental Science & Technology.title: Highly Selective Lithium Extraction from Shale Gas Wastewater Using Al- and F-Doped LiMn2O4 Electrode in Rocking-Chair Capacitive Deionization.
Environmental Science & Technology.abstract: Selective lithium extraction from shale gas wastewater (SGW) offers a promising strategy to expand lithium supply while reducing wastewater-management burdens. However, low Li+ concentrations and overwhelming competition from Na+ and Mg2+ make selective and energy-efficient extraction challenging. Lithium manganese oxide (LMO) is attractive for electrochemical Li extraction but remains limited by insufficient cycling stability and selectivity in complex ionic matrices. Here, we investigate the effects of Al and F modification of LMO on lithium extraction in a rocking-chair capacitive deionization system. Structural and spectroscopic characterizations show that the optimized modification contracts the spinel lattice and produces near-surface enrichment of F-containing species, improving electrochemical reversibility. Electrochemical analyses and density functional theory calculations further indicate favorable Li+ transport and stronger migration restrictions for Na+ and Mg2+ after lattice entry. In a simulated SGW matrix with a Li/Na/Mg molar ratio of 1:100:1, LMO-Al-F achieves a Li adsorption capacity of 9.54 mg g-1, Li/Na and Li/Mg separation factors of 2216 and 1509, and an energy consumption of 4.21 Wh mol-1 Li. Strong Li selectivity is also maintained in real SGW. After 100 competitive-ion cycles, 78% of adsorption capacity is retained, supporting repeated Li-selective extraction under high-salinity conditions.

Environmental Science & Technology.title: Water Footprint and Scarcity Risks of Low-Carbon Fuels.
Environmental Science & Technology.abstract: Production of ammonia, methanol, and hydrogen is key to decarbonizing hard-to-electrify sectors but is also water-intensive. However, the water implications of scaling these energy carriers under low-carbon pathways remain poorly understood. Here, we integrate direct water consumption with facility-level geospatial analysis and hydrological modeling to quantify water-scarcity exposure across each production facility in North America. Low-carbon production routes require more direct and indirect water consumption than conventional pathways, with electrolytic hydrogen and e-methanol increasing water-intensity by up to 5-fold in regions with limited renewable availability─a trade-off further amplified by supply chain effects, particularly for solar PV-based electricity and direct air capture-based CO2 feedstocks. Water scarcity already affects about 58% of methanol production in Mexico, 2% of ammonia production in the U.S., and 5% and 27% of refinery production in the U.S. and Mexico, respectively. Under midcentury climate scenarios, exposure increases in both magnitude and spatial extent. Although irrigation accounts for over 80% of local water consumption in various fuel production facilities, municipalities and manufacturing often exert the greatest pressure on low-carbon fuel production, depending on the product and country.. These results demonstrate that technology choice, system design, and facility siting are as important as hydrology considerations in determining water risks. Incorporating water availability in low-carbon fuel projects is therefore essential to ensure that decarbonization pathways are scalable, operationally resilient, and truly sustainable.

Environmental Science & Technology.title: Calibration of Passive Sampling Eyewear to Assess Inhalation Exposure.
Environmental Science & Technology.abstract: Calibrated wearable passive air samplers are critical tools for accessibly quantifying individualized and population exposures to airborne pollution, a leading cause of chronic disease. Our lab recently introduced passive sampling eyewear (PSE) to address gaps in tools tailored for measuring and mitigating risks from inhalation exposure. The PSE, like most existing designs of wearable samplers, is largely uncalibrated. An exception is the polydimethylsiloxane (PDMS) brooch, and mini-polyurethane foam (PUF) samplers, which have been calibrated for only 27 compounds. Here, we calibrate PSE against active air samplers codeployed in both stationary and wearable forms in office and home environments to capture a wide range of exposure scenarios. We report sampling rates (RS) and inhalation exposure for over 200 features covering diverse physical-chemical properties measured using the Orbitrap gas chromatography coupled to mass spectrometry (GC-MS) system in both targeted and nontargeted modes. RS were 0.70 ± 0.62 m3 day-1 dm-2 for stationary and 0.85 ± 0.68 m3 day-1 dm-2 for wearable deployments, with no significant difference (p = 0.06) between the deployment types. Wearable calibration captured higher RS and variability, as expected for personal sampling, because participants' movement and daily activity can alter airflow and disrupt the stagnant air-boundary layer around the sampler. In terms of analysis mode, RS derived from targeted and nontargeted analysis (NTA) were reasonably comparable for a given compound, differing by ∼1.5-fold, boosting confidence in using NTA approaches for expanding databases of RS. Applying the wearable RS, the profiles and levels of inhalation exposure varied widely between participants when at home versus in offices, reflecting differences in exposure sources and dynamics between the two environments. Overall, the findings from both the calibration and field studies represent a significant step toward quantitatively assessing inhalation exposure using PSE.

Environmental Science & Technology.title: Establishing an Air Health Index for Predicting the Risk of Acute Myocardial Infarction Onset Associated with Air Pollution and Ambient Temperature.
Environmental Science & Technology.abstract: Air pollutants and ambient temperature are important cardiovascular disease determinants, and communicating their overall risk is important for cardiovascular patient management.
