We developed a composite Air Health Index (AHI) by linking high-resolution exposure data with 1,207,625 acute myocardial infarction (AMI) cases across 325 Chinese cities. The AHI for AMI aggregates excess morbidity risks from fine particulate matter, nitrogen dioxide, ozone, and ambient temperature into a normalized scale (0-10+). Compared with existing metrics, the AHI for AMI showed better predictive performance for AMI onset than the Air Quality Index (AQI) and Air Quality Health Index (AQHI). Each interquartile range increase in the AHI for AMI was associated with a 5.97% (95% confidence interval [CI]: 5.32%-6.63%) increase in AMI incidence, surpassing the AQHI (3.33%, 95% CI: 2.93%-3.72%) and AQI (2.04%, 95% CI: 1.73%-2.35%). The AHI for AMI showed a nearly linear exposure-response relationship with no evident threshold and accounted for 8,534 per 100,000 AMI cases nationally. These associations were consistently validated in an independent external data set, supporting the robustness and generalizability of the index. In conclusion, the AHI for AMI provides an integrative and practical framework for assessing environmental health risks, offering actionable guidance for cardiovascular patient management.

Environmental Science & Technology.title: Dark Evolution of Oxalate-Derived Radicals Unlocks Sustainable Decontamination via Soil Component Interactions.
Environmental Science & Technology.abstract: We report a previously unrecognized dark aerobic pathway for radical formation from low-molecular-weight organic acids (LMWOAs)─distinct from well-documented photogenerated routes─that drives efficient soil decontamination. In ten ofloxacin-spiked soils with varying properties, oxalic acid (OA) boosted 24 h ofloxacin degradation from 20% (without LMWOAs) to 79% (7.5 mM OA), outperforming equimolar malic and citric acids. The degradation kinetics are governed by LMWOA molecular configurations─specifically, fewer carboxyl groups and lower pKa1 values that enhance reactivity─and correlate with soil organic matter (SOM) and iron contents. By combining a newly developed in situ fluorescence detector with quenching experiments, we demonstrated that in four representative soils with contrasting SOM-Fe combinations, higher Fe promotes the yields of •OH, O2•-, 1O2, and COO•-, but the coexisting SOM acts as the primary quencher. Validation experiments using artificial sand-based model soils and theoretical calculations revealed that crystalline Fe minerals (e.g., hematite), rather than dissolved Fe ions, drive radical evolution: oxalate coordinates to surface hydroxyls as a bifunctional ligand bearing electron-withdrawing carboxylates and transferable α-H, forming unstable ≡Fe(III)-oxalate complexes that undergo heterolysis and subsequent radical chain reactions, efficiently generating reactive species. Our study expands the understanding of LMWOA-derived radical geochemistry and provides a basis for nature-based, low-cost soil remediation using naturally occurring organic acids.

Environmental Science & Technology.title: Reactive Oxygen Species Trigger Rapid Natural Purification of Soils and Water in Wetlands.
Environmental Science & Technology.abstract: Wetlands, often referred to as the "Earth's kidneys", are essential ecosystems that filter pollutants and regulate biogeochemical processes. However, the mechanisms underlying their rapid self-purification are still in their infancy and lack deep understanding. Here, we propose that reactive oxygen species (ROS) constitute an intrinsic oxidative network that drives accelerated pollutant transformation in wetlands. We summarize that ROS are generated through coupled photochemical and redox-driven processes and are highly concentrated at environmental interfaces, including soil-water, fluctuating redox boundaries, and rhizosphere. These interfaces function as reactive hotspots where the colocalization of organic matter, minerals, oxygen, and microorganisms amplifies ROS production far beyond bulk water levels. Interfacial ROS enrichment can shorten pollutant half-lives and alter oxidative pathways, as illustrated by a representative pesticide. Advances in in situ and real-time ROS imaging have enabled direct observation of these microscale hotspots, providing new insights into the spatiotemporal dynamics of ROS-driven processes. We further identify key challenges in resolving and monitoring fine-scale ROS dynamics, interfacial electron transfer, and scaling microscale processes to ecosystem-level functions. This perspective reframes wetlands as interface-driven oxidative systems, highlighting ROS-mediated processes as significant regulators of pollutant transformation and providing a conceptual basis for developing wetlands as controllable biogeochemical reactors.

Environmental Science & Technology.title: Clay-Mediated Phototransformation Alters the Molecular Composition and Toxicity of Microplastic-Derived Dissolved Organic Matter.
Environmental Science & Technology.abstract: Microplastics (MPs) release complex dissolved organic matter (MPs-DOM) during environmental weathering, yet how clay minerals regulate MPs-DOM release, molecular composition, and associated biological effects remains unclear. Our study showed that montmorillonite (Mt) accelerated the photodegradation of PS and PLA microplastics, increasing the maximum release of MPs-DOM by 50.3% and 27.6%, respectively, while shifting its composition toward greater molecular complexity, fluorescence intensity, and aromaticity. Fourier transform ion cyclotron resonance mass spectrometry (FT-ICR MS) revealed that Mt altered the distribution of extractable molecular formulas, increasing the relative contribution of features within more unsaturated and oxygenated compositional regions. Quantitative analysis of reactive oxygen species (ROS) showed that the synergistic interaction between MPs-DOM and Mt influenced ROS production. Specifically, Mt increased [•OH]ss in PS- and PLA-DOM by 136.8% and 88.7%, respectively, but decreased [1O2]ss by 32.7% and 13.6%, respectively, indicating that •OH was an important contributor to molecular transformation. The Mt-amended MPs-DOM exhibited a broader profile of detectable additive-related candidates and induced greater bacterial effects than Mt-free systems. These findings demonstrate that clay minerals critically regulate the environmental fate of MPs-DOM by modulating radical generation, potentially amplifying the persistence and risks of MP pollution.

Environmental Science & Technology.title: Sustained Fe3+/Fe2+ Cycling Enables Photochemical Defluorination of Perfluoroalkyl Carboxylic Acids via Ligand-to-Metal Charge Transfer.
Environmental Science & Technology.abstract: Per- and polyfluoroalkyl substances (PFASs) are widespread persistent pollutants that threaten environmental and human health. Although Fe3+-mediated ligand-to-metal charge transfer (LMCT) has been shown to promote PFAS photochemical defluorination, existing systems rely predominantly on high-energy UV irradiation, often achieve incomplete defluorination, and generally exhibit poor performance toward short-chain and ultrashort-chain PFASs. Herein, we report a near-UV- to visible-light-driven photodefluorination strategy for perfluoroalkyl carboxylic acids (PFCAs) using commercial Fe3+ salts in acetonitrile under 405 nm irradiation, which achieved complete defluorination of long-chain perfluorooctanoic acid (PFOA) within 420 min and ultrashort-chain trifluoroacetic acid (TFA) within 240 min. Mechanistic studies combining density functional theory calculations and experimental evidence revealed that LMCT initiated decarboxylation, generating perfluoroalkyl radicals that subsequently degraded through oxidative chain-shortening reactions. The Fe3+/Fe2+ redox cycle was sustained by molecular oxygen, with hydroxyl and superoxide radicals playing auxiliary roles in reoxidizing Fe2+ and oxidizing intermediates rather than directly attacking intact PFOA. This strategy is broadly applicable to C2-C9 PFCAs, where the degradation rates are inversely correlated with chain length and are effective against perfluoroalkyl ether carboxylic acids. These findings establish a mechanistic framework for Fe3+-mediated PFAS photodefluorination in nonaqueous media and clarify the fundamental chemistry governing this process.

Environmental Science & Technology.title: Differential Risks of Incident Heart Failure Subtypes Associated with PM2.5 Chemical Constituents in China between 2006 and 2021.
Environmental Science & Technology.abstract: Despite substantial declines over the past decade, China's PM2.5 levels remain far above current WHO guidelines. PM2.5 is a recognized non-negligible risk factor for heart failure (HF), as a mixture, but the specific chemical constituents driving risks across HF subtypes remain unclear. Considering the significant heterogeneity in the etiology and pathophysiology among different HF subtypes, we explored the relationship between chemical constituents of PM2.5 and these HF subtypes. Additionally, we identified the most critical toxic constituent in the Kailuan prospective cohort of 101,521 Chinese adults followed from 2006 to 2021. Over a 14.83-year median follow-up, all chemical constituents of PM2.5 were associated with elevated risk across various HF subtypes, with notably stronger effects on early onset compared to late-onset HF. Moreover, black carbon (BC) (40.2%-48.7%) was the main contributor to overall HF, late-onset HF, and HF with reduced ejection fraction (HFrEF) and mildly reduced (HFmrEF), whereas NH4+ (28.2%) and BC (28.1%) primarily drove early onset HF, and OM (34.8%) was the key constituent for HFpEF. Chronic exposure to specific-constituents of PM2.5 increases various HF subtypes risk, underscoring the importance for regional and constituent-specific regulations to alleviate HF burden.

Environmental Science & Technology.title: Nitrous Acid Formation in Wildfire Plumes: Implications for Atmospheric Oxidation and Ozone Pollution.
Environmental Science & Technology.abstract: Nitrous acid (HONO) is a vital precursor for hydroxyl (OH) radicals in wildfire plumes, yet chemical transport models often underrepresent observed in-plume HONO levels. We implemented wildfire HONO emissions and literature-based secondary formation pathways in the Weather Research and Forecasting model coupled with Chemistry (WRF-Chem) and evaluated simulations against airborne measurements from the Fire Influence on Regional to Global Environments and Air Quality (FIREX-AQ) campaign during 2019 summer wildfires in the northwestern United States. The revised model substantially improves in-plume HONO representation. Source attribution revealed that emissions contributed up to 40% of HONO in near-source smoke, while heterogeneous NO2 uptake on aerosol surfaces acted as the dominant pathway (47%-74%) due to the dense reactive surface area of smoke aerosols. HONO photolysis accounted for approximately 80% of the primary OH production in the near-field smoke, identifying HONO as the leading primary radical-initiation pathway during this stage of plume evolution. HONO-initiated radical production further accelerated radical cycling, yielding a net increase in O3 concentrations both near the surface and at the plume transport altitude. Our findings underscore the pivotal role of HONO in driving smoke-plume chemical evolution and highlight its importance for assessing regional air pollution and tropospheric O3 burdens.

Environmental Science & Technology.title: Evaluating the Effect of China's Pesticide Guidance Actions on Soil Ecological Risks Based on Spatiotemporal Pesticide Input Dynamics from 2001 to 2050.
Environmental Science & Technology.abstract: A national action, titled the Zero Growth of Pesticide Use Action Plan (ZAP), was launched to tackle pesticide pollution risks by the Chinese government in 2015, leading to substantial reductions in pesticide inputs. However, the effect of such a national action on risk mitigation remains unknown. This study characterizes the spatiotemporal dynamics of pesticide inputs and risks of 146 pesticide active ingredients across China from 2001 to 2022 and provides projections up to 2050 to evaluate the efficacy of ZAP under a moderate future climate change scenario. A transition in pesticide input was observed from 2001 to 2022, revealing a redistribution of hotspots from the North China and Yangtze River basins to more widely distributed locations in southern China. Despite the overall reduction in quantities used, pesticide concentrations doubled in soils from 2001 (1.04 mg kg-1) to 2022 (2.25 mg kg-1), with pesticide residues in soils becoming more persistent. The launch of ZAP in the short term (from 2015 to 2022) decreased the applied mass of hazardous pesticides. From the long-term view, a reduction of pesticide inputs exceeding 50% is projected to be achieved with herbicide inputs continuously increasing. By mode of action, protoporphyrinogen oxidase inhibitors and photosystem I electron diverters contributed disproportionately to soil ecological risk. Consequently, a delayed risk mitigation effect was observed: the proportion of croplands at medium risk fell from 85% in 2015 to 70% in 2050. Our analysis calls for integrated measures toward precise pesticide management, including sustainable plant protection and pollution remediation.

Environmental Science & Technology.title: Evaluating Individual Infection Risk: The Interplay between Air Mixing Intensities and Occupant Dynamics.
Environmental Science & Technology.abstract: Aerosol transmission remains a critical route for the spread of respiratory infectious diseases, yet real-time exposure mapping in complex public spaces is computationally demanding. This study presents a robust and adaptable framework for estimating dynamic individual exposure (i.e., viral dose) by integrating high-fidelity computational fluid dynamics (CFD) with computer vision (CV) analysis. By overlaying validated steady-state viral aerosol plumes onto dynamic human interaction data, we evaluated the interplay between airflow patterns and human behaviors under two distinct air change rates (ACH: 25 h-1 and 3 h-1). Each scenario was simulated both with and without MERV-13 filtration. Applications in both a stochastic-movement hotel meeting room and a stationary-occupant office demonstrate that while high turbulence due to high ACH limits the spatial extent of plumes, sustained close proximity in structured settings can result in disproportionately high viral doses for specific individuals. MERV-13 filtration effectively reduced exposure within high-concentration zones. We propose a Reynolds number (Re)-based modeling guideline: steady-state CFD-CV for moderate mixing (900 ≤ Re ≤ 2300), a well-mixed assumption for high mixing (Re > 2300), and transient CFD-CV for low mixing (500 ≤ Re < 900) during breathing and speaking, and steady-state CFD-CV for coughing and sneezing regardless of Re value. This framework supports real-time monitoring and targeted interventions, providing a data-driven foundation for indoor occupant safety.

Environmental Science & Technology.title: Atmospheric Aging Modifies the Toxicological Profile of Biomass Burning Particles in Epithelial Lung Cells.
Environmental Science & Technology.abstract: Wildfire activity and associated smoke emissions are increasing globally, leading to widespread exposure to biomass burning particulate matter (PM). Although people are mainly exposed to aged wildfire smoke rather than fresh emissions, the effects of atmospheric aging on wildfire particulate toxicity remain poorly understood. Here, we investigated how atmospheric processing ("aging") modifies biological effects of biomass burning particles (BBPs) generated under controlled flaming and smoldering combustion conditions. BB emissions were produced in the Photochemical Large Aerosol Chamber (PHOTO-LAC) and aged under alternating photochemical and dark conditions. Fresh and aged BBP extracts were subsequently sampled and tested in human bronchial epithelial cells (BEAS-2B). We assessed cytotoxicity, oxidative stress, oxidative DNA damage, genome-wide transcriptional responses, and inflammatory and extracellular matrix-related protein expression. Atmospheric aging substantially altered BBP toxicity in a combustion-dependent manner. Aged BBP enhanced intracellular reactive oxygen species formation and oxidative DNA damage, particularly for smoldering emissions, while cytotoxicity remained largely unchanged. In contrast, inflammatory and matrix-remodeling responses were attenuated with aging in smoldering particles but remained stable for flaming BBP. These findings demonstrate that atmospheric aging can simultaneously amplify oxidative and genotoxic stress while dampening inflammatory signaling, underscoring the need to incorporate aging state into health risk assessments of wildfire smoke exposure.

PLOS Biology.title: Dynamic functional connectivity reveals evolving neural activity states of alcohol-seeking in rats
PLOS Biology.abstract: by Yujing Zhang, Nicholas M. Timme, Mintao Liu, Christopher C. Lapish, Joaquín Goñi The brain mechanisms underlying persistent alcohol-seeking in Alcohol Use Disorder (AUD) remain incompletely understood. To investigate this behavior, we characterized the temporal evolution of neural activity states in the anterior cingulate cortex of freely behaving rats performing an aversion-resistant drinking (ARD) task. Alcohol-preferring (P) rats were assessed, as they reliably exhibit ARD when alcohol is devalued with the bitter tastant quinine. P rats were compared with Wistar rats, which progress slower to ARD, as indicated by cessation of drinking following quinine devaluation. Using dynamic functional connectivity analyses of spike-train recordings, we identified latent neural states corresponding to seeking and non-seeking phases. We then integrated the latent-state decoding of neural activity with a seeking intensity model derived from the observed drinking behavior. This framework revealed that the decoded latent neural states closely tracked behavior. Furthermore, during alcohol-reinforced sessions, neural and behavioral measures of drinking or non-drinking states were strongly aligned in both strains. However, after alcohol devaluation, this alignment diverged in P rats but remained consistent in Wistars. The inability of P rats to acquire stable neural states following devaluation suggests impaired formation of latent states as a neural mechanism of ARD, offering insights into the cognitive vulnerabilities that may sustain AUD.

Genome Biology and Evolution.title: Generative continuous time model reveals epistatic signatures in protein evolution.
Genome Biology and Evolution.abstract: Protein evolution is fundamentally shaped by epistasis, where the effect of a mutation depends on the sequence context. As standard phylogenetic methods assume independently evolving sites, there is a need for more complex models based on accurate estimations of the fitness landscape. Good candidates are modern generative models - such as the Potts model - which successfully capture epistatic effects. However, recent works on generative evolutionary models usually use discrete time, making them difficult to integrate with the standard frameworks in evolutionary biology. We introduce a continuous-time sequence evolution model using the Gillespie algorithm and parameterized by a generative Potts model. This approach enables us to simulate realistic, family-specific evolutionary trajectories and allows for direct comparison with independent-site models. Surprisingly, we find that while epistasis significantly slows down evolution, it does not change the average evolutionary rates at individual sites. This is explained by the rate heterogeneity caused by context-dependence: we show that the rate at some positions varies between null to high values depending on the context, while other positions are essentially independent from the context. Finally, we show that epistasis leads to a systematic underestimation bias in the inference of evolutionary distance between sequences. Overall, our work provides a new tool for simulating realistic protein evolution and offers novel insights into the complex interplay between epistasis and evolutionary dynamics.

Nature Water.title: Time for water to take centre stage
Nature Water.abstract: Nature Water, Published online: 17 November 2026; doi:10.1038/s44221-026-00762-2Transforming the water agenda requires a shift to more inclusive governance, greater community empowerment and a stronger focus on foresight, alongside the recognition of water’s central role in addressing society’s greatest challenges.

Nature Water.title: Water innovation-sharing must become a tool for peace-building
Nature Water.abstract: Nature Water, Published online: 17 November 2026; doi:10.1038/s44221-026-00746-2Water innovations such as desalination, wastewater reuse and rainwater harvesting can do more than strengthen water security. International cooperation is needed to ensure that these technologies promote equitable benefit-sharing, mobilize investment and reduce tensions in regions where climate stress and water scarcity threaten stability.
